correctness.rationale: The two strict half-plane conditions are exactly the open sector of half-angle pi/4. Principal squaring gives every positive-real-part Carathéodory function, and the analytic logarithmic primitive realizes the reverse implication. At r=3/5 the exact pullback disk identity is v^2(v^6+12v^4+21v^2+46)/4 on the target parabolic boundary; all factors are nonnegative and equality forces q=1/2. Connectedness and the inclusion of 1 settle all nonreal boundary points without numerical sampling. The extremal q=sqrt((1+z)/(1-z)) reaches q=1/2 at z=-3/5 and fails immediately beyond. A separate checker verifies all rational coefficients.

value.rationale: The 2026 focal question asks for a sharp radius of parabolic starlikeness. The natural two-sided spirallike constraint at opposite pi/4 angles is precisely a classical full strong-starlikeness order-1/2 family; its largest universal parabolic radius increases sharply from the ordinary starlike value 1/3 to 3/5. A global algebraic tangency identity identifies why no nonreal contact occurs and an explicit normalized extremizer proves sharpness. The exact reverse quantitative relationship between two standard shape classes is intrinsically useful, not an arbitrary finite computation.
